title: Dedicated capacity SLA: verifiable metrics, error-budget definitions, and customer notice templates
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define a verifiable, auditable SLA for Dedicated capacity customers that ties measurable serving metrics to a clear error-budget burn model and a contract-ready set of customer notice and credit templates. Deliverables: (1) metric definitions and instrumentation requirements, (2) error-budget computation and burn categories, (3) remediation ladder + credit computation, (4) customer-facing notice templates and legal-friendly clause snippets.
background: Customers on Dedicated pools request predictable throughput guarantees with transparent remediation. Existing documents cover throughput bands and credit math but lack a single, auditable metric set and ready-to-send notice templates. This causes engineering/legal thrash during renewals and incident response. We need a reproducible SLA artifact the Console and Billing systems can use for automation.
proposed_solution: Adopt a dual-metric SLA: Guaranteed Serve Rate (GSR) measured as tokens-per-minute 99th percentile across the customer's committed window, and a Degradation Index (DI) measured as sustained percent below committed GSR over N-minute windows. Use weighted error-budget burn combining frequency (count of violations) and severity (percent below). Automate detection in telemetry and wire up to billing to auto-issue credits when thresholds are met. Ship customer notice templates for pre-notice, outage notice, and credit issuance.
metrics: Guaranteed Serve Rate (GSR): tokens/min at 99th percentile measured per customer per AZ during customer's entitlement window (configurable). Requires per-tenant token counters and synchronized windowing in telemetry.
Degradation Index (DI): rolling percentage deficit vs committed GSR measured over 5/15/60 min windows. DI = max(0, 1 - observed_gsr/committed_gsr).

Availability floor: percentage of time the service returns successful responses for requests under committed model-type (e.g., generation vs embeddings). This is a secondary signal used for fallbacks and legal definitions.
error_budget_formula: Daily error budget (EB) expressed in 'token-minutes' = committed_tokens_per_minute * entitlement_minutes * allowed_degradation_fraction. Burn for an incident = sum_over_windows((committed_gsr - observed_gsr) * window_minutes) for windows where observed_gsr < committed_gsr. Remaining EB = EB - burn.
credit_formula_examples: Example 1: 10k tpm committed over 60 minutes (entitlement_minutes=60), allowed_degradation_fraction=0.05 => EB = 10,000 * 60 * 0.05 = 30,000 token-minutes.
Incident: a 15-minute window where observed_gsr=8k tpm => burn = (10k-8k)*15 = 30,000 token-minutes => EB exhausted => triggers credit per schedule.

Credit computation: proportional credit = min(100%, burn/EB_window) * monthly_commitment_value * credit_multiplier (default 1.0). For the example above, if this incident consumes the monthly window EB, credit = monthly_commitment_value * 1.0 * (proportion of month impacted).
contract_language_snippets: Service Commitment: Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to provide the Customer with a Guaranteed Serve Rate (GSR) equal to or greater than the committed tokens-per-minute for the Dedicated pool during the Customer’s entitlement window.

Measurement and Verification: GSR and Degradation Index (DI) shall be measured by Redwood’s telemetry pipeline. The Customer may request a measurement export for auditing within 30 days of an incident. Disputed measurements will be resolved per the Dispute Resolution appendix.

Remedy: If Redwood consumes the Customer’s error budget for a billing period, Redwood will issue a proportional service credit computed per the Credit Computation formula in Appendix A. Credits are the sole financial remedy for SLA violations.
notification_templates:
Pre-Notice (to Customer): Subject: Potential Dedicated Capacity Degradation - [Customer] - [Pool]
Hello [Customer Contact],
We’re seeing early indicators that the Dedicated pool serving your environment may experience degraded throughput. Our engineering team is investigating. We will send a follow-up within 30 minutes with actions and ETA.
- Redwood Inference NOC

Incident Notice: Subject: Incident: Dedicated Throughput Degradation - [Customer]
Hello [Customer Contact],
At [timestamp], we detected sustained degradation below your committed GSR. Impact: [summary]. Mitigation: [actions, e.g., autoscale triggered, fallback model enabled]. We estimate recovery ETA: [ETA]. We will publish a post-incident report and, if the measured burn exceeds your error budget, apply credits per the SLA.
- Redwood Inference NOC

Credit Issuance Notice: Subject: SLA Credit Issued - [Customer]
Hello [Customer Contact],
Following verification of the incident on [date], Redwood has applied a service credit of [amount] to your account per the Dedicated Capacity SLA. Details and calculation are attached. Contact your Customer Success rep with questions.
- Redwood Inference Billing
remediation_ladder: Tier 0 (Automatic): Smart autoscaler attempts burst provisioning within 60s when queue/backpressure metrics exceed threshold. No customer notice unless sustained for 5 minutes.
Tier 1 (NOC + Customer): If degradation persists >5 minutes, NOC opens incident and sends Incident Notice. Autoscale policy runs with pre-provisioned spare nodes in same AZ.

Tier 2 (Cross-AZ failover): If persistent >15 minutes or hardware loss in AZ, route traffic to warm standby AZ based on routing policy. Customer may elect to absorb cross-AZ latency impact or request manual failover.

Tier 3 (Credit and Escalation): If error budget is exhausted for billing window, finance/billing issues proportional credit within 7 business days and account lead engages for RCA and remediation plan.
rollout_plan: 1) Finalize metric definitions and telemetry instrumentation spec (ENG + Observability) - target 2 weeks.
2) Implementation spike to validate per-tenant counters and windowing (ENG) - 1 sprint.
3) Billing wiring: define final credit API and automated issuance flows (Finance/Platform) - 2 sprints.
4) Legal sign-off on clause snippets and notice templates, then include in Dedicated contract addendum - 1 week.
5) Pilot with 2 strategic customers and iterate on notification cadence and credit math - 4 weeks.
6) GA release and Console UI for SLA status + historical burn visualization - 2 sprints.
Rollout note: start with a conservative allowed_degradation_fraction (5%) and tighten as telemetry proves reliability.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Telemetry exports per customer for GSR and DI are available and reproducible via query with documented windowing semantics.
A2: Error budget computation matches examples and is validated against historical incidents in staging.
A3: Automated credit issuance can be triggered and audited end-to-end in staging with sample account.
A4: Customer-facing notice templates approved by Legal and Customer Success and stored in Drive.
A5: Pilot customers sign off on SLA measurement and notification cadence before GA.

postmortem_and_risk_notes: Risk: false positives due to window alignment across AZs. Mitigation: require cross-AZ quorum for GSR violations and provide raw telemetry for customers. Risk: credit model complexity causing disputes — mitigation: keep initial credit multiplier = 1.0 and provide worked examples.
